laws.historical_context: Lebanon's primary civil law code, adopted during the French Mandate. Modeled on the French Civil Code (Code Napoleon of 1804) and the Ottoman Mecelle, but adapted for Lebanese specificities. Known as the 'COC' among Lebanese law students. Covers general obligations, contracts, torts, property transactions, and specific nominate contracts. Notably excludes personal status matters (marriage, divorce, inheritance) which are governed by each religious community's own laws. The COC remains the backbone of Lebanese private law and is the most frequently cited code in Lebanese civil courts.
laws.notes: The COC was originally published in French and Arabic. French doctrine and jurisprudence are frequently cited by Lebanese courts when interpreting its provisions. A complete English translation was published by Gabriel M. Bustros (Bureau of Lebanese and Arab Documentation, 1970).

laws.historical_context: Replaced the earlier Code of Civil Procedure. Issued as a decree-law during the Civil War period when Parliament was not functioning regularly. Governs all civil and commercial litigation procedures including jurisdiction, service of process, evidence, judgment, appeals, and execution. The arbitration chapter has gained particular importance for Lebanon's role as a regional commercial center.

Established the modern Lebanese property registration system (Torrens system). Replaced Ottoman land law categories. Created the Land Registry system still in use today. Governs ownership, servitudes, usufruct, and real property rights.

amendments.summary: Post-war rent law establishing rent control and tenant protections.

New comprehensive rent law replacing previous framework. Introduced gradual rent increases for pre-1992 tenancies over 9-12 year transitional period. Created Rent Committee and Fund for tenants. Partially suspended by Constitutional Council Decision No. 6/2014 and subsequently amended.

laws.historical_context: Lebanon's rent laws have been among the most politically contentious areas of legislation. Exceptional rent laws freezing rents for pre-1992 tenancies were enacted during and after the Civil War, creating a dual market between 'old rent' (heavily protected tenants) and 'new rent' (market-rate). The 2017 law attempted to gradually liberalize old rents over a transitional period but faced legal challenges and implementation difficulties.

Governs the structure and function of the Lebanese judiciary. Establishes the hierarchy of ordinary courts: courts of first instance, courts of appeal, and the Court of Cassation. Also establishes the Supreme Judicial Council headed by the First President (Chief Justice) of the Court of Cassation. Defines jurisdiction of civil, criminal, and commercial chambers at each level.
